mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has stabilized near -70 to -72 over the last two weeks after a sharp initial drop, indicating the lockdown-induced floor has been reached. Absent new shocks, this plateau will persist, keeping RETAIL_REC roughly flat to slightly negative over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC values -63.7,-71.9,-70.6,-71.7 show convergence to a floor
failure_condition: If mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days rises by more than 5 points relative to the last 28 days, the plateau hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility remains persistently elevated (22.4 to 26.3 percent above baseline) across all four weeks, consistent with strict stay-at-home enforcement under England's third national lockdown announced in early January 2021. As long as this policy regime holds, retail and recreation trips will remain suppressed or decline further over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed above +22 for four consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL falls below +15 while RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises, indicating policy relaxation, the suppression mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility falls further by more than 10 points week-on-week from its current -71.1 level, it signals a tightening of movement restrictions or reduced essential travel capacity, which would mechanically reduce access to retail and recreation destinations within 2 weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 10 points week-on-week from -71.1
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at t-0w is -71.1, close to its t-2w trough of -75.6
failure_condition: If TRANSIT declines sharply but RETAIL_REC does not fall correspondingly within 2 weeks, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous suppression of WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility compounds to reduce incidental retail trips normally made during commuting (e.g., lunch breaks, errands near transit hubs). When both series are deeply negative together, the combined effect depresses RETAIL_REC more than either alone, over a 4-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES below -50 and TRANSIT below -65 simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -55.4 and TRANSIT at -71.1 in the latest week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining jointly depressed, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: January is a low-daylight, cold-weather month in London; the recent decline in PARKS mobility (from -17.1 to -30.7) reflects seasonal weather suppression of outdoor activity rather than policy change. This seasonal effect will continue to modestly suppress overall discretionary mobility, including RETAIL_REC, over the next 1-2 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined from -17.1 at t-3w to -30.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS mobility recovers or RETAIL_REC rises despite continued PARKS decline, the seasonal co-movement mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp rise in RESIDENTIAL and corresponding drop in GROCERY_PHARM volatility (settling near -30 after an initial swing from -16.1 to -32.0) suggest households have adapted to essential-only shopping routines. This behavioral adaptation implies continued restraint in discretionary retail visits over the next 2 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stabilized near -30 after initial volatility
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL remain stable but RETAIL_REC rises more than 5 points, the behavioral-restraint hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM mobility rises above -20 (toward baseline) while WORKPLACES remains deeply negative, it would indicate selective policy easing for essential retail without broader reopening, which would only modestly lift RETAIL_REC due to continued restrictions on non-essential venues.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -20 while WORKPLACES stays below -50
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises as described but RETAIL_REC does not increase within 2 weeks, the selective-easing mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The oscillation in RETAIL_REC and PARKS between t-1w and t-0w (-70.6 to -71.7 and -27.4 to -30.7 respectively) without a clear directional trend suggests behavioral fatigue has reached equilibrium, with no new systematic push toward higher or lower mobility over the next 4 weeks absent an external shock.
evidence_refs: fact:both series show small week-on-week oscillation rather than trend in the last two weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC exhibits a clear upward trend exceeding 5 points over the next 28 days relative to the prior 28 days, the equilibrium-fatigue hypothesis is rejected.
